newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends mixed after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends mixed after choppy session.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures ended lower after a choppy session that found sentiment trapped between conflicting inventory expectations and technically-motivated trading by speculators, dealers said.

Products ended mixed in equally volatile trade. Heating oil futures finally settled lower while unleaded gasoline fought off mid-afternoon declines to firm in the spot month as well as in several outer months.
July crude settled at $21.59 a barrel, down 31 cents, after whipsawing between a high of $22.15 and a low of $21.53. The spot June contract went off the board at $21.19, down 40 cents.
July heating oil fell 0.38 cent to end at 57.67 cents a gallon, but June unleaded gasoline (still more active than July) settled 0.18 cent higher at 65.39 cents a gallon.
News was scarce, with rumors (unconfirmed and unsupported by cash market activity) about cat cracker difficulties supporting the gasoline market, one trader said.

Although the crude market was clearly jittery about the this week's inventory report after receiving a shock in last week's numbers, most action was led by disintegrating spot-month prices as the June paper expired, traders said.

"Who ever knows for sure what the stats are going to bring," one broker said. "All the pressure was on the June crude, and with all the talk about declining European refining margins and overseas demand backing away, no one feels too strongly about it," he said.
The crude trading was marked by heavy selling - termed "feverish" by one dealer - toward the close as speculators and funds fought to unload June positions, traders said.
"They couldn't sell the (June/July) spread, (the spread) blew out to 50 points, and by the end they were selling the June outright," one dealer said.
He said funds were still long but that another 20- to 30-cent drop in July would push them out of their positions.

The complex was controlled at the opening by speculators and funds who were trying to push values lower in an attempt to break through key technical support levels, as well as complete the liquidation of the expiring June crude contract, according to floor traders.

Failing that, the compelex reversed and pushed for new highs, which was also unsuccesful. Midday action became lackluster until conflicting estimates for weekly inventory figures began to create volatility, traders said.

The weekly inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute was due after the close. A survey of traders and analysts conducted by Reuters showed most expecting falling crude stocks, but dealers were trading on calls for a build in crude stocks of two to three million barrels.
"The cash (traders) were putting out estimates for builds (in inventory) across the board" in crude, heat and gas," one floor broker said.
